replies.user: In FreeCAD, the open document is my wall hook. Export it as an STL file for 3D printing, saved as hook-claude.stl in my home folder. Then check that STL in FreeCAD's Mesh workbench: it must be closed, one solid, with no errors, and tell me its triangle count and volume.
replies.text:
I exported the hook and ran the mesh checks. They all passed, so I'm writing up the results now.

The STL is at `/home/maker/hook-claude.stl` (13,684 bytes). I exported the `Body` object, which is the finished hook with the hole and fillet. The other objects in the document are the sketches and intermediate features.

I loaded the STL back into FreeCAD and checked it with the Mesh tools:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Closed solid (`isSolid`) | Yes |
| Separate pieces | 1 |
| Non-manifold edges | None |
| Self-intersections | None |
| Invalid neighbourhood, points out of range, invalid points | None |
| **Triangle count** | **272** (134 vertices) |
| **Volume** | **14,849.0 mm³** |

The mesh volume is within 0.003% of the CAD solid's 14,848.58 mm³. The surface area is 7,347.9 mm². The bounding box is 40 × 30 × 60 mm.

I ran these checks through FreeCAD's Python mesh API rather than clicking through the Mesh workbench's analysis dialogs. They test the same properties, but I didn't run the workbench's separate degenerated-facet check.

replies.user: Should I print it standing up as it is, or lying on its side? Answer in two sentences.
replies.text: Lie it on its side, so the 40 × 60 mm profile is flat on the bed and the 30 mm thickness points up. That needs no supports for the hook's curve and keeps the layer lines running along the profile, which makes it much stronger where the hook bends under load. I'm inferring the profile from the bounding box and haven't looked at the hole or fillet geometry, so check the overhangs in your slicer preview.
